questions.statement: Which word in English names the subject where students work with numbers and solve problems?
questions.context: In a classroom in Pereira, the teacher writes the names of the subjects on the board.

options.text: Math.
options.feedback: Math is the subject where students work with numbers and solve problems.

options.text: Art.
options.feedback: Art is the subject where students draw, paint, and use colors.

options.text: Science.
options.feedback: Science is the subject where students learn about nature and experiments.

options.text: Music.
options.feedback: Music is the subject where students sing and play instruments.

questions.explanation: Identifying basic school subjects by their main content in English (math, art, science, music). / Identificar asignaturas basicas segun su contenido en ingles.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why does Sofia like science class?
questions.context: Read: "On Monday, Sofia has science class. She likes it because she learns about plants and animals."

options.text: Because she learns about plants and animals.
options.feedback: The text directly says she learns about plants and animals in science.

options.text: Because she draws pictures with colors.
options.feedback: Drawing pictures is part of art class, not science.

options.text: Because she plays soccer with her friends.
options.feedback: Playing soccer is part of physical education, not science.

options.text: Because she sings songs in English.
options.feedback: Singing songs is part of music class, not science.

questions.explanation: Understanding the reason a student likes a subject from a short text in English. / Comprender la razon por la que un estudiante prefiere una asignatura.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses a preposition of time with days of the week?
questions.context: A student talks about her week: "I have art class on Tuesday and Friday."

options.text: We have math class on Wednesday.
options.feedback: The preposition "on" is used before days of the week in English.

options.text: We have math class in Wednesday.
options.feedback: "In" is used with months and years, not with days of the week.

options.text: We have math class at Wednesday.
options.feedback: "At" is used with clock times, not with days of the week.

options.text: We have math class to Wednesday.
options.feedback: "To" is not a preposition of time for days of the week.

questions.explanation: Using the correct preposition of time with days of the week in English. / Usar la preposicion de tiempo correcta con los dias de la semana.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question correctly matches this answer about school subjects?
questions.context: A teacher asks: "What is your favorite subject?" A student answers: "My favorite subject is science."

options.text: What is your favorite subject?
options.feedback: The answer names a favorite subject, so this question fits perfectly.

options.text: What time do you have lunch?
options.feedback: The answer does not talk about lunch or any time of day.

options.text: How many brothers do you have?
options.feedback: The answer does not talk about family members.

options.text: Where do you live?
options.feedback: The answer does not mention a home or an address.

questions.explanation: Matching questions with answers about school subjects in English. / Relacionar preguntas con respuestas sobre asignaturas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly describes the schedule?
questions.context: A student in Villavicencio reads her schedule: "Monday: math at 7:00. Tuesday: science at 8:00. Wednesday: art at 9:00."

options.text: She has science class on Tuesday at 8:00.
options.feedback: The schedule shows science on Tuesday at 8:00.

options.text: She has art class on Monday at 7:00.
options.feedback: The schedule shows math on Monday at 7:00, not art.

options.text: She has math class on Wednesday at 9:00.
options.feedback: The schedule shows art on Wednesday at 9:00, not math.

options.text: She has science class on Friday at 10:00.
options.feedback: Friday is not in the schedule, and science is on Tuesday.

questions.explanation: Reading a simple class schedule and using days and times correctly in English. / Leer un horario simple y usar dias y horas correctamente.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: On which day does Andres have both math and science class?
questions.context: Read: "Andres has math class every day. He has science class only on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. He has art class only on Tuesday."

options.text: On Monday.
options.feedback: Math is every day, and science is on Monday, so both happen on Monday.

options.text: On Tuesday.
options.feedback: Science is not on Tuesday; Andres has art class that day.

options.text: On Thursday.
options.feedback: Science is not on Thursday, so he only has math that day.

options.text: On Sunday.
options.feedback: There is no class on Sunday, so no subject is scheduled.

questions.explanation: Analyzing schedule information to find when two subjects happen on the same day. / Analizar un horario para hallar cuando dos asignaturas coinciden el mismo dia.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which comparison correctly explains why Valentina practices more English than Mateo?
questions.context: Compare two students: "Valentina has five English classes every week, but Mateo has only two. Valentina also practices English at home."

options.text: Valentina has more English classes and practices at home.
options.feedback: Her extra classes and home practice explain her greater practice.

options.text: Mateo has five English classes and practices at home.
options.feedback: The text says Mateo has only two classes, not five.

options.text: Valentina has fewer English classes than Mateo.
options.feedback: The text says Valentina has more classes than Mateo.

options.text: Neither Valentina nor Mateo studies English.
options.feedback: Both students have English classes, according to the text.

questions.explanation: Comparing school schedules in English to explain differences in practice. / Comparar horarios en ingles para explicar diferencias de practica.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the most important message of this paragraph?
questions.context: Read: 'A good school schedule has subjects like math, science, art, and English on different days. It also gives students time to rest and play, so they can learn better every week.'

options.text: A good schedule combines different subjects with time to rest and play.
options.feedback: The text links varied subjects and rest time with learning better.

options.text: Students should study only one subject all week.
options.feedback: The text says a good schedule has different subjects, not only one.

options.text: Rest and play are not useful for learning.
options.feedback: The text says rest and play help students learn better.

options.text: School schedules should not include English classes.
options.feedback: The text includes English among the subjects in a good schedule.

questions.explanation: Evaluating the main message of a short expository paragraph about school schedules. / Evaluar el mensaje principal de un parrafo sobre horarios escolares.
questions.subject: ingles
